text:
Noah Li: Auditor emailed asking for an evidence package covering one 24h window: RBAC changes, KMS usage, and a small vuln-triage crosswalk. They want chain-of-custody links (change -> approver -> PR) plus 3 example decrypt traces. Any objections to the scope?
Jasmine Riley: Fine scope. We should avoid including any customer identifiers. Recommend: redact emails -> keep stable hashed ids, include PR numbers, and only include encryptedDataKey blobs (no plaintext).
Connor Zhang: Agreed. For RBAC I'll pull k8s rolebinding events and Okta/SCIM provisioning diffs. I'll output rbac_changes.csv with fields: change_id, principal_hash, change_action, resource, pr_ref, approver, utc_ts.
Aisha Khan: On KMS: CloudTrail has Decrypt/GenerateDataKey and DescribeKey. Export matching events and key metadata snapshots. Include GetKeyRotationStatus output. We'll never include key material.
AuditorBot: Please provide 3 end-to-end samples that map PR -> rolebinding -> service-account -> KMS Decrypt requestId. Hash principals but keep timestamps and requestIds intact.
Noah Li: Good. Let's standardize hashing: `user_sha256:<hex>` and `sa_sha256:<hex>`. Document the hash algorithm in README.
Jasmine Riley: Splunk query I'll run:```
index=audit OR index=cloudtrail
(eventType="RoleBinding" OR eventName="Decrypt" OR eventName="GenerateDataKey" OR source="scim")
| where _time>=strptime("2025-02-12T00:00:00Z","%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") AND _time<strptime("2025-02-13T00:00:00Z","%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
| table _time,eventType,eventName,principal,resource,requestId,requestParameters,responseElements
```
Connor Zhang: After export I'll canonicalize to ISO8601 UTC and run the hashing script. I'll also create change_mapping.csv linking change_id -> pr_ref -> approver -> deploy_ts.
Aisha Khan: For KMS, include fields: _time, eventName, keyId, requesterPrincipal (hashed), requestId, encryptedDataKey (base64), responseElements. Also include DescribeKey JSON snapshots and rotation status.
AuditorBot: Include a signed manifest with SHA256 for each file and GPG signature. Auditor requires signer identity and fingerprint.
Noah Li: Use key `audit-sec@redwood` to sign. Add signature and fingerprint to README. Also include instructions for verifying the signature.
Jasmine Riley: Redaction rules in README: 1) replace email/login with `user_sha256:...`; 2) replace SA names with `sa_sha256:...`; 3) drop any `customer_id` fields unless LOA provided; 4) keep requestIds and timestamps.
Connor Zhang: Vulnerability crosswalk: I'll produce vuln_crosswalk.csv with columns: vuln_id, service, pr_fix, fixed_at_utc, severity, public_cve. No stack traces or PII.
Aisha Khan: Packaging plan: zip -> redwood_evidence_2025-02-12.zip, files: rbac_changes.csv, kms_events.ndjson, key_snapshots.json, change_mapping.csv, vuln_crosswalk.csv, MANIFEST.txt, README.md. MANIFEST.txt includes sha256 for each file and a GPG signature file MANIFEST.txt.asc.
Noah Li: Timeline? Auditor wants delivery by EOD Wednesday. Can we hit that?
Jasmine Riley: I can run exports tonight and upload to secure S3 bucket.
Connor Zhang: I'll run the hashing and assemble package tomorrow morning.
Aisha Khan: I'll gather key metadata and do the manifest signing once bundle is ready.
AuditorBot: Also request: short 20-minute walkthrough to show Splunk query results and sample trace linking. Please propose a time.
Noah Li: How about Thurs 9:30-9:50am PT for a quick walkthrough?
Jasmine Riley: Works for me.
Connor Zhang: I'm available.
Aisha Khan: I'll join.
Noah Li: OK I'll send invite and will attach presigned S3 link + MANIFEST sha256 once built. Reminder: do not hand over any logs with raw emails. If auditor asks for unredacted samples, require LOA.
AuditorBot: Confirmed. Please include the manifest sha256 in the calendar note.
Noah Li: Will post the link and manifest hash here when uploaded. Thanks team :thumbsup:
